newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly chief quits over accidents.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly chief quits over accidents.

text.p: The president of Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp has resigned in the face of strong public and political pressure after a spate of accidents, including a deadly gas explosion on Monday.
The Ministry of Economic Affairs, which oversees the state-run company, said on Wednedsay that president Chen Kuo-young had tendered his resignation late on Tuesday.
"He informed the ministry on Tuesday night that he wants to resign," a ministry official told Reuters by telephone.
Chen's resignation was expected to be approved on Wednesday, the ministry official said.
A Chinese Petroleum official who asked not to be identified told Reuters that company vice president Roy Chiu was most likely to succeed Chen.

Chen's resignation came a day after a gas explosion at the company's Taoyuan refinery killed a worker, the latest in a series of accidents that have raised questions about Chinese Petroleum's safety procedures.

The accidents -- more than a dozen this year including fires, oil leaks on land and offshore -- have caused costly shutdowns of the Taoyuan refinery, its crude port and other facilities and caused the oil giant some US$40 million in compensation.

Economics minister Wang Chih-kuang told reporters on Tuesday that if an investigation showed Monday's blast was caused by human error or faulty management, Chen and chairman Chang Tzu-yuan "would have to be punished".

Chang has faced intense pressure from opposition political parties, who have made him a target in their attacks on the ruling Nationalist Party, but he has shown no indications that he might step down.
Trying to take the upper hand, Chang has pledged to find and punish who if anyone was responsible for the explosion.
Initial inspection reports said the accident was caused by a gas leak without indication of human error.
